content.text:
**Observations**

- Dead (never‑updated) input rows are easy to spot: they still hold the untrained pattern 0.020, 0.030, 0.050 … 0.530. Mapping them to pixel positions: row 0 is dead except cols 12–15; row 1 is dead at cols 0–3 and 24–27; rows 2–5 lose only 1–4 pixels at each end; rows 6–22 are essentially fully alive (only an occasional col 0/27 pixel is dead); rows 23–26 lose 2–3 pixels at each end; row 27 is alive at cols 4–23. So only the four corners (≈60–70 pixels in total) are never lit; objects reach the top, bottom, left and right borders.
- Large |W1| values are *not* in the centre of the image. The strongest weights sit near the borders: a broad band in rows 1–4, cols 8–26 (unit 15 ≈ +0.3…+0.43, units 6/10/11 ≈ −0.3…−0.43, unit 4 ≈ +0.3…+0.41 along row 2 cols 19–27); a very strong vertical strip at the right edge, cols 20–25, rows 7–22 (unit 0: +0.40/+0.52 at rows 9–10 flipping to −0.56/−0.65/−0.72 at rows 11–13; unit 15 the opposite sign; units 4, 1, 9 ≈ ±0.3…0.44 down col 23–24 to row 22); a strip at the left edge, cols 1–7, rows 12–21 (unit 7 +0.4…+0.52 at rows 15–17, units 1 and 8 ≈ −0.3…−0.4 at rows 12–20); and a broad band in rows 23–25, cols 3–22 (units 2, 3, 5, 6 ≈ +0.25…+0.44, units 9, 12 ≈ −0.3…−0.4). The central region (rows 8–20, cols 8–18) mostly carries weights |w| < 0.2.
- Weights vary smoothly along horizontal runs (e.g. unit 4 ≈ 0.31, 0.28, 0.33, 0.37, 0.36, 0.38, 0.32, 0.29 across consecutive columns in row 2) and along vertical runs down the side strips — i.e. the units respond to the *outline* of a filled shape (where its top, sides, bottom are), not to strokes in the middle.
- Hidden units thus look like silhouette detectors: "mass at top‑centre vs. not" (15, 6, 10, 11), "mass at the right edge in rows 7–10 but not rows 11–13" (0 vs 15 – a sharp horizontal boundary at the right edge about row 10/11), "right edge filled down to row 22" (4, 1, 9), "left edge filled in rows 15–20" (7, 8, 1), "wide bright band at the bottom" (2, 3, 5, 6 vs 9, 12).
- Left/right asymmetry: the right‑hand strip (cols 20–25) is far stronger than the left one, so the data themselves are systematically asymmetric.
- W2 is dense with entries of ±0.3…1.07; every class draws on many units, and classes form groups that share signs (e.g. unit 4: +0.86 for class 7, −0.89 class 4, −0.63 class 2; unit 5: +0.82 class 2, −0.84 class 0, −0.81 class 8; unit 9: +0.93 class 4, −0.86 class 9, −0.73 class 5; unit 15: + for 2, 6, 8, − for 4, 7, 3, 5). Biases are small.

**Reasoning**

- Handwritten‑character data (MNIST, EMNIST, KMNIST) are ruled out: there the digit sits in a 20×20 box, rows 0–3 / 24–27 and cols 0–3 / 24–27 are (almost) never lit, so their weights would stay near initialisation, and the discriminative weights would be concentrated in the centre. Here it is the reverse: rows 1–4 and 23–25 and the side columns carry the biggest, most structured weights, while the centre is comparatively flat. Only the corners are dead.
- That pattern — objects that fill the frame top‑to‑bottom, interiors that are uniformly filled (hence uninformative), class information carried by the outline (shoulders/collar at the top, sleeves or lack of them at the sides, hem/sole at the bottom) — is exactly what a linear‑ish model learns on Fashion‑MNIST. The sharp sign flip at the right edge between rows 9–10 and rows 11–13 is the kind of feature that separates short sleeves (T‑shirt) from long sleeves (pullover/coat/shirt), and, because all Fashion‑MNIST shoes point left with heel/shaft on the right, the same right‑hand region separates a tall ankle‑boot shaft from a sneaker's low heel collar and a sandal's open straps — explaining the strong left/right asymmetry. The wide bright bottom band is where soles and hems lie; top‑centre weights pick up collars, waistbands and bag handles (the only things that ever reach row 0, cols 12–15).
- The grouping in W2 (e.g. coat/pullover share signs against T‑shirt/dress/trouser; the three footwear classes behave jointly on several units) is consistent with the 10 Fashion‑MNIST categories rather than with 10 digits, which would not produce such edge‑driven features.

**Dataset:** Fashion‑MNIST (Zalando 28×28 grayscale clothing‑article images, white item on black background).

**Classes:** 0 T‑shirt/top, 1 Trouser, 2 Pullover, 3 Dress, 4 Coat, 5 Sandal, 6 Shirt, 7 Sneaker, 8 Bag, 9 Ankle boot.

**Confidence:** 72%
